clue.text: Bishop leading one religious group that's equally split

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
the Roman numeral I stands for one
a sect is a religious faction

explanation.surface: A bishop heads a congregation that is divided down the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading' just places the bishop's B at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut something into two matching halves is the verb's exact meaning, used of lines and angles in geometry.

clue.text: Small animal found under gooseberry?

explanation.surface: A tiny creature turns up beneath a fruit bush.
explanation.walkthrough: British nursery lore tells children that babies are found under a gooseberry bush; the bush and the baby together give the small African primate.
explanation.definitionFit: A small nocturnal African primate (galago) carries this name; the second reading is the baby said to be found under a gooseberry bush.

clue.text: Main section required for naval manoeuvres

definitions.text: Main section required for naval manoeuvres

parts.words: Main section required for naval manoeuvres
parts.note: the main is the open ocean, and a ship needs a stretch of it clear around her to turn and manoeuvre safely

explanation.surface: A principal part of something is needed for warships to perform exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' reads as 'principal' but is the old word for the open ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The term means space at sea clear of hazards in which a vessel can manoeuvre.

clue.text: Sweet child at home with one composer

parts.note: a cherub is an angelic, sweet-faced child
in means at home
the Roman numeral I stands for one

explanation.surface: A lovely youngster stays in with a lone musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Luigi Cherubini was an Italian composer of operas and sacred music who worked in Paris.

clue.text: Prepare to shoot bird as soon as one can see

definitions.text: as soon as one can see

parts.note: to cock a gun is to raise its hammer ready to fire
a crow is a black bird

explanation.surface: A hunter readies the gun for a bird at first light.
explanation.definitionFit: The time when roosters call is dawn, the moment it first becomes light enough to see.

clue.text: Poet and economist provided site for this educational establishment

definitions.text: Poet and economist provided site for this educational establishment

parts.words: Poet and economist provided site for this educational establishment
parts.note: the poet Milton and the economist Keynes together name the English new town where this distance-learning institution has its headquarters

explanation.surface: A writer of verse and a money theorist donated land for a college.
explanation.walkthrough: Milton Keynes is a new town in Buckinghamshire, England, home of the distance-learning university founded in 1969.
explanation.definitionFit: The UK's distance-learning institution, open to students without entry qualifications, is based in Milton Keynes.

clue.text: Pirate captain initially young, just a child

parts.note: Captain William Kidd was a notorious Scottish pirate

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of the word young

explanation.surface: A buccaneer chief was once only a boy.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiddy is an informal, affectionate word for a small youngster.

clue.text: Fur-seal on the rocks? No

indicators.note: something on the rocks is wrecked, so the letters of the clue word are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A marine mammal basking on a reef, followed by a curt negative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rocks' paints a seal basking on a shore but signals a rearrangement of FURSEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying no is a denial or rejection of a request.

clue.text: Wife that is least slim

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife in genealogies
id est is the Latin for that is, abbreviated i.e.

explanation.surface: A spouse is said to be the stoutest of all.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadest is the superlative of broad, the opposite of slim.

clue.text: Negligible amount, something to shove and throw around

parts.note: a halfpenny is the coin pushed across the board in shove-ha'penny, a British pub game

indicators.note: around tells us to jumble the letters of throw

explanation.surface: A trifling quantity of something you can push and fling about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is the anagram signal on 'throw'. Shove-ha'penny is a British pub game in which old coins are pushed up a board; 'shove' looks like a verb of pushing about.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worth only a half-penny is a tiny, trivial quantity.

clue.text: Old friend in impasse

parts.note: stale means old and no longer fresh
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: A long-standing pal caught in a deadlock.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock where neither side can make progress, from the chess position with no legal move.

clue.text: Face up to Duke, backing one of the old county set

definitions.text: one of the old county set

indicators.note: backing means the word for face up to is read from the end to the start

parts.note: to defy is to confront or face up to

explanation.surface: Someone confronts a nobleman, supporting a member of the landed gentry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns the whole run DEFYD round. Dyfed was a Welsh county from 1974 to 1996; 'county set' sounds like the landed gentry.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyfed was one of the Welsh administrative regions abolished in 1996.

clue.text: Live with old composer, say, producing epic

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

indicators.note: say signals that the composer's name is to be spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: Hugo Wolf was an Austrian composer of songs

explanation.surface: A musician lives alongside an elderly composer and creates a grand work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks the sound of WOLF, spelt WULF.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old English heroic poem about the slaying of Grendel is the great Anglo-Saxon saga.

clue.text: Novel name for Civil War hero

explanation.surface: An unusual name for a hero of the American Civil War.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' reads as 'new' but is the noun: James Joyce's book.
explanation.definitionFit: James Joyce's novel bears the name, and it was also the first name of Union general Ulysses S. Grant.

clue.text: Animated creature in book with limited scope

indicators.note: limited means the word for scope is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: ambit means range or scope

explanation.surface: A lively animal appears in a book of narrow range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limited' trims AMBIT to AMBI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Disney cartoon fawn is the most famous creature of film animation.

clue.text: Way-out method of making predictions?

parts.note: an eccentric forecasting technique on the surface, but literally a survey taken at the way out of a polling station

explanation.surface: An outlandish system of forecasting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Way-out' reads as weird but means at the exit.
explanation.definitionFit: Voters are surveyed as they leave the polling station to forecast an election result.

clue.text: Supply bound copy of book

parts.note: supply reads as a verb, but here it means in a supple way: a book with a flexible, soft binding

explanation.surface: Provide a bound edition of a volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' is not the verb but supple plus -ly: bound softly, as opposed to hardback.
explanation.definitionFit: A softcover edition has a flexible card binding rather than stiff boards.

clue.text: Damn! Life can make one so hot and bothered

indicators.note: can make says the letters of the two words are rearranged to form something new

explanation.surface: An exasperated curse: life can make anyone flustered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can make' rearranges DAMN and LIFE.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflamed means heated and angry, worked up into a passion.

clue.text: Musical work one can play

explanation.surface: A piece of music anyone can perform.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilbert and Sullivan wrote an operetta of this name, and it is also the card game for a single player.

clue.text: Vehicle included in any financial support separately provided

indicators.note: included in places the vehicle within the letters of the word any

parts.note: a limo is a limousine, a luxury car

explanation.surface: A car is part of a maintenance package arranged independently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'separately' hints at separated spouses.
explanation.definitionFit: Maintenance paid to an ex-spouse after a divorce or separation.

clue.text: Shellfish from river caught by man on board

indicators.note: caught by puts the river's letter within the chess piece

parts.note: a pawn is a chessman on the board

explanation.surface: A crustacean taken from a river by a sailor on deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man on board' suggests a sailor; it is a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A small edible decapod crustacean, a type of seafood.

clue.text: Pleasantness of quarters, surrounded by friendship

indicators.note: surrounded by places the compass quarters inside the word for friendship

parts.note: amity means friendship
E and N are two of the compass quarters, east and north

explanation.surface: The agreeableness of a lodging enclosed by goodwill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarters' suggests lodgings but means compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means agreeableness of a place or manner, as in the amenity of a setting.

clue.text: Saint initially bored stiff

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of the word bored

parts.note: rigid means stiff

explanation.surface: A holy figure is at first bored to death.
explanation.definitionFit: St Brigid of Kildare is one of Ireland's patron saints.

clue.text: Colourful display from artist in London area

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
Bow is a district of East London

explanation.surface: A colourful show by a painter in part of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is a district of East London, home of the Bow Bells.
explanation.definitionFit: The arc of seven colours in the sky after rain is nature's spectrum show.

clue.text: Singers in opera perch on one

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the fish above the numeral

parts.note: the bass is a fish of the perch family
the Roman numeral I stands for one

explanation.surface: Opera performers sit atop a single stool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perch' suggests a seat but is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian plural of basso, the lowest male voices in opera.

clue.text: Carriage prematurely stopped by a new driver? Bizarre

indicators.note: prematurely stopped means the carriage word loses its last letter

parts.note: a surrey is a light four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage
L is the learner plate on a car driven by a new driver

explanation.surface: A coach halted early by a novice motorist seems dreamlike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prematurely stopped' cuts SURREY to SURRE. In Britain learner drivers display an L plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreamlike and strange, in the manner of Dalí's art.

clue.text: Grand polar explorer was extremely fat

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars
James Clark Ross was a British explorer of the Arctic and Antarctic

explanation.surface: A great Arctic adventurer was hugely overweight.
explanation.definitionFit: Gross describes someone obese, disgustingly large in body.

clue.text: Interest in ceremonies, some spiritual, is mystical

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some feel that devotion to rites is spiritual and mystical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes RITUALISM from spi(RITUAL IS M)ystical.
explanation.definitionFit: A devotion to formal rites and liturgy, especially in church worship.

clue.text: Clear distance from robbery, sort of

explanation.surface: A wide gap separates someone from a theft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daylight robbery' is British slang for an outrageous overcharge.
explanation.definitionFit: Visible space between things, as between racing horses; and the word that comes before robbery in the phrase for blatant overcharging.

clue.text: Allowed to include girl's name in dictionary

indicators.note: include means the dictionary's letters go around the girl's name

parts.note: the OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
Kay is a female first name

explanation.surface: Permitted to put a woman's name into a reference book.
explanation.definitionFit: Okayed means approved or sanctioned, given the go-ahead.
